title: TesseraQL code catalogs v1
description: Schema for TesseraQL catalog documents (catalogs/*.yml): small, nearly static tables of codes and the names they stand for, loaded whole and resolved from memory. Documented in code-catalogs.md.

catalogs.description: Named catalogs. Files merge into one app-wide namespace, and a name declared twice is a build error.

table.description: The table the codes live in. Exactly one of table: or file: — a catalog reads one source.

file.description: A SQL file under catalogs/ whose result set is the catalog, for a shape table:/where: cannot express — codes in one table and their per-language names in another. The SQL owns its own filtering and ordering, so where:/order: are refused beside it.

tables.description: With file:, the source tables the SQL reads. This is what lets a maintenance command's invalidates: reach the catalog without anything having to parse SQL, so it is required with file:.

where.description: Equality filters pinning this catalog's slice of a shared code master. A general master holds every kind of code keyed by a type column; fixing the type here is what makes the catalog itself single-keyed, so a field domain can reference it. The values are bound, never interpolated.

key.description: The column carrying the code. With file:, it names a result column of that SELECT.

label.description: Where the name comes from: a result column, or a message-catalog key with the code interpolated. The message form puts the names in the translation workflow the Studio message editor already serves and adds no per-language table.

message.description: The key, with {key} replaced by the code — for example code.priority.{key}. The load then says only which codes exist, and each becomes one entry per locale the app supports.

language.description: An optional column carrying the BCP-47 tag a row's name is written in. Language is a dimension of the catalog rather than part of its key, so the call site is the same in every language and only the labels differ; an untranslated code falls back to the default language, never to the raw code.

order.description: An optional display-order column deciding the order a form offers the codes in. A column rather than a sort by label, because label collation is locale-dependent and code masters already carry one.

active.description: An optional column whose truth marks a code still offered and accepted. It does not affect resolution: names resolve over every row, so a retired code still renders on last year's data and is simply not offered on today's form.

datasource.description: The named connector the catalog loads from, defaulting to main.

cache.description: How long a load is held before the source is read again.

maxAge.description: A duration such as 1h (the default) or 15m. Underneath it sit a maintenance command's invalidates: and the validation path's re-read, so the hold is a display delay and never a wrong rejection.
